lastText: File ClosedThe Republic's Last AddressMajor DefeatItalian High Command, 1940–1945End of hostilities: APRIL 28, 1945 · filed late, out of sequenceImmediate AftermathThe Italian Social Republic ends on April 28, 1945, twenty months after Mussolini's rescue from Gran Sasso installed it as a German client state in the occupied north. The human cost of this path runs higher than the historical one at nearly every hinge point: Italy's own wartime dead, roughly 300,000 military and civilian combined split across two governments and a country fought over twice, were already among the higher tolls of any Axis power relative to population. Mussolini's answer to Romania was delayed rather than rushed: the single change every honest account of the Greek campaign says should have been made, and on this path, was. The delay meant to buy Rome a coordinated defense instead bought German intelligence two additional days to reinforce the garrison: Operation Achse executed even more completely than its historical version. A deliberate early withdrawal from the Alamein line concedes the same ground the historical twelve-day battle eventually lost anyway, without first spending the attritional casualties a fuel-starved defense was never favored to hold.
